newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL rises on results on bearish market.
newsitem.headline: MOL rises on results on bearish market.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mostly lower on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday, defying expectations for an overall rise on the market.
The BUX index finished at 3,581.00 points, up 8.25.

"Today's session caused some surprise," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities. "One expected the whole market to rise after the Federal Reserve left its interest rates unchanged and also one expected a more serious rise after MOL's results."
Despite bullish expectations after good nine-month results, shares of oil and gas company MOL closed only 30 forints higher, at 1,650, below the day's peak of 1,670.
Lencs was not particularly optimistic about the bourse's short-term outlook saying the market apparently ran out of steam and became unable to take advantage from positive news.
"I don't think we could expect signficant rises or falls in the near term, the market will be flat," he said.
Shares of other companies releasing January-September results today, traded mixed.
Tile manufacturer Zalakeramia closed at 6,800 forints, down 50, while spirits maker Zwack remained untraded.
On Thursday trading was suspended in the shares of research and development company Horizon-Multiplan.
The BSE decided to suspend trading in the shares to protect the interest of investors who may have not received important information about the company's expected 1996 results.

On Thursday two Hungarian dailies published Horizon-Multiplan business figures based on the company's statement, while the official bourse gazette received the information too late to publish it on Thursday.
